notes.title: Version 2.2.3 Patch Notes
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Optimized movement within the dungeon for a smoother experience.
[*] Fixed an issue where entering a Tunnel of Wishes during Parallel Play occasionally caused the boss not to appear.
[*] Fixed an issue where players who did not purchase DLC content were unable to delete the downloaded rescue request for a DLC-exclusive dungeon.
[*] Fixed an issue where high frame rate processing caused the app to speed up and induce control difficulties in certain areas.
[*] Addressed an issue where save data could become corrupted due to various events, such as force-quitting the app at certain times, loss of system power,etc.
[*] The mouse cursor now becomes hidden when the screen mode is set to either Borderless or Full Screen.
[*] 12 other miscellaneous fixes and adjustments.
[/list]

*Balance adjustments have not been made.

notes.title: Shiren the Wanderer: The Mystery Dungeon of Serpentcoil Island review
notes.content: The decades-old Shiren the Wanderer series is famous for being bluntly unforgiving, and The Mystery Dungeon of Serpentcoil Island is no exception to that intimidating rule. I'm dumped into a randomised dungeon and expected to fend for myself using nothing more than whatever I find lying around on the floor, the stairs to the next level only promising more of the same pain. A monster strolls into the room, one tile at a time, and I freeze, carefully considering every step and sword swing I can make before I act... Read more.

notes.title: Shiren the Wanderer's simple graphics disguise a systems-dense roguelike full of the emergent stories I love the genre for
notes.content: Shiren The Wanderer didn't quite invent the traditional roguelike genre, but this long-running, rarely localized Japanese series sure as heck came to define it:.. Read more.

notes.title: Rejoice, roguelike nerds: Shiren the Wanderer: The Mystery Dungeon of Serpentcoil Island is coming to Steam
notes.content: "It shouldn't be this hard to play the best version of one of Japan's great roguelikes today," PC Gamer contributor Kerry Brunskill wrote earlier this year in a retelling of her long fight to get her hands on a PC copy of 2002's Shiren the Wanderer: Monster of Moonlight Village. She also expressed hope that the latest game in the series, the Nintendo Switch-exclusive Mystery Dungeon of Serpentcoil Island, would eventually make its way to PC. Good news for Kerry—it's on the way, and you won't have to get someone in Japan to mail it to you... Read more.
